name: ai.mysiren/siren
title: Siren
description: Deterministic visual marketing engine. Your agent plans, renders, and posts on-brand campaigns.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description:
Get the connected Siren workspace: plan, key scopes, auto-post
setting, and daily limit. Call this first to learn what the account
can do before generating. Empty asset_types / channels /
connected_accounts lists mean UNRESTRICTED, not missing — never stop
on them. Films render on every plan; credits are the only meter.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description:
List the workspace's generation runs (newest first): status, brief,
channel, asset URLs, and caption. Page with offset to see them all.

limit.description: How many runs to return, 1 to 50. Newest first.

offset.description: Skip this many runs, to page back through every video and image the workspace has made.

tools.name: get_run
tools.description:
Get one run by id — full status, output text, asset URLs,
caption, and any error. Poll this after create_campaign
or render_asset until status is terminal. Wait `poll_after_seconds`
between polls; `progress` and `eta_seconds` say how far along it is.
A finished film carries `film_check`, advice only: when `ok` is
false, show the human the video and the findings and let them decide.
Re-render at most once, and only for a defect you can name in what you
sent (a missing image, a wrong name). `notices` are plain-words notes
on the request (e.g. it asked for a mood the brand's look does not
wear): the asset is made as asked; pass the note to the human. A
finished run carries `caption`: the post caption Siren wrote in the
run's brand (or yours, if you passed one); show it with the asset. After
post_run, `posts[]` carries each platform's status and, once it
fires, the live URL and the caption that went out.

run_id.description: The run id returned by create_campaign, render_asset, or list_runs.

tools.name: create_campaign
tools.description:
Create a Siren campaign from a plain-language brief — the full
pipeline: plan, on-brand copy, deterministic render, verify. Returns
the run; pass callback_url to be pinged when it ends, or poll get_run until it finishes. Spends credits (image 10, an ad set of 3 images 20,
video 25; voice or music-only is the same 25). Pass output_type to
pin a film (list_films has the catalog); omit it and Siren picks.
Optional scheduled_at (ISO-8601)
queues a sequential post (X → Instagram → TikTok, or platforms you
pass) when the render succeeds — requires Allow posting. Fails with
a 402 upgrade message if the plan or balance can't cover it.

FILM KNOBS: voiceover (true narrated / false music only), direction
(mood, pace, motion, music in one line), music (a bed id), media
(upload_media URLs the film shows). Images ignore the film knobs:
Siren writes and paints them from the brief and Brand DNA.

ANY BRAND: pass `brand` to make it for a brand that is not this
workspace's own, e.g. brand={"name": "Acme", "site": "acme.com",
"logo_url": "https://acme.com/logo.png", "primary": "#FF4400"}.
Nothing of this workspace's identity leaks in.

The exact same request within 24 hours returns the run it already
started, as it is now, with replayed=true and no new charge. Change
the brief to make another.

brief.description: Plain-language request for the post, e.g. "announce the new export feature, use the dashboard screenshot".

channel.description: Omit to cut one render per connected platform, up to the credit balance and the plan cap (Spark stops at 2). Pass twitter, instagram, linkedin, tiktok, or youtube for a single cut. A shape named in the brief wins: square, vertical, portrait, story, wide, landscape, 4:5, 9:16, 16:9.

asset_type.description: What to make: card (still image) or video.

output_type.description: Optional film to pin, e.g. "story" or "pitch". Call list_films to browse; describe_film for the contract. Omit and Siren picks the format from the brief.

caption.description: Optional caption for the post this run becomes. Your words are kept; omit and Siren writes the caption.

scheduled_at.description: ISO-8601 time to post, e.g. 2026-09-12T09:00:00. Interpreted in the given timezone.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name for scheduled_at, e.g. Africa/Lagos or America/New_York.

platforms.description: Where to post: any of x, instagram, tiktok, linkedin, youtube, or ["everything"] for every connected channel.

voiceover.description: Films: true = narrated in the brand voice, false = motion + music only. Omit and the brief decides; if the human never said, ask them once.

direction.description: Films: one free line on mood, pace, motion and music, e.g. "emotional, slow, soft piano" or "dark, club energy, fast cuts".

music.description: Films: a music bed track_id. Omit and the bed follows the film and the direction.

media.description: Films: URLs from upload_media (images and videos) for the film to show. Omit and the film shows the brand's recent work. Images (asset_type=card): photos from upload_media are painted into the creative as given, placed where the brief says ("our mug in the top-left"); videos are refused for images.

variants.description: Images only. 3 makes an ad set: the same creative with three different headlines, for testing hooks on paid feeds. 20 credits for the three instead of 10 for one. get_run then returns all three in asset_urls. Default 1.

brand.description: Make it for ANOTHER brand instead of this workspace's own (a client, a brand people recognise, a side project). Object: {name (required), site, logo_url (https PNG/SVG/JPG of the brand's MARK or app icon, e.g. Duolingo's owl, not the wordmark: the film sets the name in type), accent (hex: the brand's signature colour, the one films are painted in), primary (hex: its dark or ink colour), secondary, tagline, font (the brand's typeface name, e.g. Nunito), x_handle, sells (one line: what they make)}. Clean slate: none of this workspace's logo, colours, mascot, font, handle, screenshots or memory is used; only what you send. YOU look the brand up first: their site, their logo file (the image in their site header, or their /brand or /press page, or the app icon) and their colours as hex. A missing, dead or damaged logo is refused (brand_logo_required / brand_logo_unreachable / brand_logo_unreadable) because a film with no mark is a generic video; one colour for both primary and accent is refused too. Never invent a logo URL and never pass a screenshot of their page as the logo. Omit to use this workspace's Brand DNA.

callback_url.description: Instead of polling: an https URL Siren POSTs to once when the run ends, with event run.completed (asset_url, caption) or run.failed (error). Signed with callback_secret: Standard Webhooks headers (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature) plus X-Signature-256 (hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body). If your harness can make a webhook address for you, pass it here and wait for the ping.

callback_secret.description: Secret for the callback signature, 16 to 200 characters. Omit and Siren mints one, returned once as callback_secret.

tools.name: list_films
tools.description:
The film library, one ranked page at a time. Films sit on job
shelves; pass job and the human's goal and hire from the top of the
page. Each film says what it is, when to hire it, its length and
shapes, fits_this_brand (with what is missing) and made_recently
(this brand already got it: prefer another film on the shelf unless
the human asked for that one). Page on with next_page. Want it all at
once? all=true, or fetch the catalog file (https://api.mysiren.ai/api/v1/films.md,
every film by shelf, also .txt/.json) and read it in steps. search=
finds films by word. Then describe_film for the body. Videos are on every plan;
credits are the only limit. Every film here is 25 credits. Platinum films (50 credits) are
not in these pages: the answer's platinum section flags them, and
list_platinum_films has the shelf.

job.description: The shelf: launch, feature (one feature or update), explain (what the product does), brand (story, manifesto, mood), ai (AI or agent product), proof (a number, testimonials), app (mobile app), shop (products, food, property), people (team or mascot). Omit to rank the whole library.

goal.description: The human's own words for the outcome, e.g. "launch video for our new AI agent" or "show our 10k users". Ranks the films by fit.

page.description: Page number, from 1. Each page is page_size films; next_page in the answer says what to call next.

max_seconds.description: Only films this long or shorter, e.g. 15 for a short feed post.

narrated.description: true = only films with a voice-over part; false = only music-and-motion films.

aspect.description: Only films that render this shape: wide-desktop, square-ig, story-reel, vertical-ig-feed.

detail.description: "short" (default) or "full" to add the long description per film.

search.description: Find films by word across ids, names and descriptions, e.g. "phone", "chat", "mascot", "halftone". Every word must match.

all.description: true = every film that passes the filters on one page (about 10k tokens for the whole library). Prefer job + page, or the catalog.md file.

for_brand.description: The brand name you will pass in create_campaign brand_override, when the video is for a brand other than this workspace. fits_this_brand then judges that brand (no mascot, people or screens of this workspace).

tools.name: list_platinum_films
tools.description:
The platinum shelf: studio-grade films that match a top motion
studio's craft, told as the brand's own story. Each costs 50 credits,
every time (a normal film is 25). Offer one only when the human is
making a big launch they genuinely want to go far; everyday posts and
normal budgets use list_films. Say the price before you render. Ids end
in -plt. Platinum needs a paid plan or a credit top-up: a complimentary
plan sees it but gets 402 platinum_needs_paid_plan. voice MM = motion and music only (no voice-over question, no
narration); MVM = motion, voice and music. Then describe_film for the
body, same as any film.

tools.name: list_styles
tools.description:
The still style library, one ranked page at a time. Every painted
still (an ad creative, poster, release card, App Store frame,
thumbnail) is one style; Siren picks one when you don't. Styles sit
on section shelves; pass section and the human's goal and take one
from the top. made_recently = this brand already got that look,
prefer another. To paint in a style, put its id in the
create_campaign brief (asset_type card). The whole library as one
file: https://api.mysiren.ai/api/v1/styles.md (also .txt/.json).

section.description: The shelf: social-ad (feed ads), poster, launch, brand, og (link previews), youtube (thumbnails), app-store, event, wallpaper, arts-creative, premium (flagship posters: the brand mark as a lit object). Omit to rank the whole library.

goal.description: The human's own words for the still, e.g. "a hot take about launches" or "our pricing is simple". Ranks the styles by fit.

page.description: Page number, from 1. next_page in the answer says what to call next.

search.description: Find styles by word in their id or when-to-pick line, e.g. "comic", "receipt", "billboard".

aspect.description: Only styles that paint on this shape: square-ig, vertical-ig-feed, story-reel, wide-desktop.

all.description: true = every style that passes the filters on one page. Prefer section + page, or the styles.md file.

tools.name: describe_film
tools.description:
The full contract for one film: what it is and when to hire it, its
body JSON Schema, a reference body, the seed envelope, media slots
(which fields take image/video URLs), the brand prefills (colours,
logo, screens) and the override rules. Call it before writing a
render_asset body.

tools.name: clarify_brief
tools.description:
Ask Siren's clarifier whether a brief is specific enough to
generate from. Returns ready=true/false plus follow-up questions.
Use before create_campaign when the user's request is vague.

brief.description: Plain-language request for the post, e.g. "announce the new export feature, use the dashboard screenshot".

tools.name: render_asset
tools.description:
Render films from pre-formed SirenSeed bodies (advanced). FILMS ONLY:
images are painted from a brief, so for any image, ad or creative call
create_campaign with asset_type=card (a still here returns 422
stills_use_a_brief). Each item: {output_type, channel,
seed_body, archetype?, family?, surface?, caption?, voice_id?,
music?, direction?, brand_override?}. Prefer create_campaign unless
the user has concrete seed JSON. Returns run ids, `estimated_seconds`
and `poll_after_seconds`; wait that long, then get_run, or pass
callback_url and Siren pings it once per run when each ends.

THE DIRECTOR: every film body is edited against Brand DNA before it
renders. It keeps the film and your brand-specific lines, rewrites
empty, generic or reference-body copy, and never touches media.
`director` in the response says what changed. `direction` is a free
line ("dark, club energy, fast") that steers words, pace and music.
A film that cannot use what you sent returns 422 film_does_not_fit
with a `fix` and `films_that_fit`.

ANY BRAND: put brand_override={"name": "Acme", "site": "acme.com",
"logo_url": "https://acme.com/logo.png", "primary": "#FF4400",
"accent": "#111111"} on an item to render it for a brand that is not
this workspace's own. With a name it is a clean slate: none of this
workspace's logo, mascot, font, handle, screenshots or stills are used.
Media slots take only URLs you uploaded with upload_media.

items.description: Pre-formed SirenSeed film bodies to render (films only; images go through create_campaign). Each item: {output_type, channel, seed_body, archetype?, family?, surface?, caption?, voice_id?, music?, direction?, brand_override?}. music = a bed track_id (omit and the bed follows the film and brand). direction = one free line that steers words, pace and music. brand_override with a name = render for ANOTHER brand, clean slate: {name, site, logo_url, primary, accent, secondary, tagline, font, x_handle}.

name.description: Human-readable name for the asset or run.

callback_url.description: Instead of polling: an https URL Siren POSTs to once when the run ends, with event run.completed (asset_url, caption) or run.failed (error). Signed with callback_secret: Standard Webhooks headers (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature) plus X-Signature-256 (hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body). If your harness can make a webhook address for you, pass it here and wait for the ping.

callback_secret.description: Secret for the callback signature, 16 to 200 characters. Omit and Siren mints one, returned once as callback_secret.

tools.name: upload_media
tools.description:
Store a photo or video the human wants in a post, from an https URL
or base64. Returns a workspace-owned URL to put in any media slot of a
film body (describe_film lists the slots) — the renderer reads it
directly. Images: PNG/JPG/WebP up to 15 MB. Videos: MP4/MOV/WebM up
to 200 MB. The same bytes are stored once (content-hashed).

url.description: Public https URL of the photo or video to store. Pass this or base64.

base64.description: The media bytes as base64, if you have no URL. Pass this or url.

kind.description: auto (default), image, or video. Detected from the bytes when auto.

tools.name: edit_asset
tools.description:
Edit a finished ad creative in place. Only what the instruction
names changes; faces, layout, lettering and every other pixel are
kept, so you can chain edits (hair pink, then tail teal, then add a
sign) without the picture drifting. About 15 seconds. 3 credits; an
instruction that asks for a whole new look ("make it a comic",
"make it cinematic") repaints at 10. Returns the NEW run: poll get_run
until it is terminal and show the human the new image. Films are not
edited this way: re-render them with render_asset. Every earlier
version stays, so the human can go back to any of them.

run_id.description: A finished ad creative (painted still) to change: the run id from create_campaign, get_run or list_runs.

instruction.description: What to change, in plain words: "make her hair pink", "swap the mug for a laptop", "fix the spelling of the headline". Name one or two changes; everything else stays.

tools.name: post_run
tools.description:
Post a finished run's assets to the workspace's CONNECTED SOCIAL
ACCOUNT. This is live, public distribution on the customer's channel
— always confirm with the user before calling. Only works if the
grant was authorised with posting allowed. Pass `caption` to own the
words; it goes out verbatim. The call queues the post behind a short
publish window (about two minutes, cancellable) rather than firing
inline: poll get_run after that and read `posts[].url` for the live
permalink and the caption that went out.

run_id.description: The run id returned by create_campaign, render_asset, or list_runs.

platform.description: Connected channel to post to: x, instagram, tiktok, linkedin, or youtube.

caption.description: Optional caption for this publish; goes out verbatim. Omit and Siren writes it.

tools.name: schedule_post
tools.description:
Schedule a finished run to post at scheduled_at (ISO-8601).
Shows in the customer's local timezone. platforms: x, instagram,
tiktok, linkedin, youtube, or everything. Posts fire sequentially.
Requires Allow posting. Prefer this over post_run when the user
names a time. On create_campaign you can pass scheduled_at instead.

run_id.description: The run id returned by create_campaign, render_asset, or list_runs.

scheduled_at.description: ISO-8601 time to post, e.g. 2026-09-12T09:00:00. Interpreted in the given timezone.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name for scheduled_at, e.g. Africa/Lagos or America/New_York.

platforms.description: Where to post: any of x, instagram, tiktok, linkedin, youtube, or ["everything"] for every connected channel.

captions.description: Optional caption override per platform, e.g. {"x": "...", "linkedin": "..."}.

tools.name: get_brand_dna
tools.description:
Get this workspace's Brand DNA: brand_name, brand_kind, overview,
tagline, offer, features, products, audience, palette, logos, plus
`checks`: what to fix before rendering (thin Brand DNA, a typed
accent the brand's own work does not use). Call right after
get_account; fix thin DNA first with update_brand_dna and
upload_product_screen, or ask the human for the site. Not Brand
Memory.

tools.name: update_brand_dna
tools.description:
Patch Brand DNA. Send only keys to change. Nested bags (offer,
product_map, icp) merge. Examples: {tagline, overview,
offer: {product_name, one_liner, features, who_its_for, primary_cta},
product_map: {offerings, how_we_work}, icp: {who_buys, pains},
colour_use: {primary, secondary, accent} (when each colour should be
the ground, e.g. {"accent": "loud ads that must stop the scroll"}),
mark_faces: right | left | none (which way the logo looks)}.
Does not read or write Brand Memory.

fields.description: Brand DNA keys to change, e.g. {"tagline": "...", "offer": {"one_liner": "..."}}. Nested bags merge.

tools.name: list_product_screens
tools.description:
List the brand assets in Brand DNA: product photos, app screenshots,
packaging. Each row has name, kind, description, use_when, tags,
scan_status (scanning / ready / failed), device, theme, url.

tools.name: upload_product_screen
tools.description:
Upload a brand asset (product photo, app screenshot, packaging) into
Brand DNA and store it on R2. Pass image_url (https PNG/JPG/WebP) or
image_base64.

Two ways to file it:
- Send `description` (and optionally kind, use_when, tags, name): Siren
  trusts your words and files the asset as-is. No read.
- Send only the file: Gemini reads the picture and writes name, kind,
  description, use_when, tags itself. scan_status goes scanning → ready
  in about 8 seconds; poll list_product_screens.

kind is free text ("product photo", "dashboard screenshot", "packaging"),
there is no fixed list. A brief that names an asset ("advertise the
pink handbag") pulls that file into the still. screen_type / device /
theme only matter for device-framed screenshot masters.

image_url.description: Public https URL of a PNG, JPG, or WebP to store as a brand asset.

image_base64.description: The image bytes as base64, if you have no URL.

name.description: Human-readable name for the asset or run.

description.description: What the picture shows and what it is for, in your words. When set, Siren files the asset without reading it.

kind.description: Free-text kind: product photo, dashboard screenshot, packaging, logo, team photo.

use_when.description: When Siren should reach for this asset, e.g. "any post about the analytics page".

tags.description: Short lowercase tags for search, e.g. ["dashboard", "dark-mode"].

screen_type.description: Screen role: feature, hero, onboarding, settings, or marketing.

device.description: Device the screenshot was taken on: phone, tablet, desktop, or none.

theme.description: UI theme in the screenshot: light, dark, or unknown.

tools.name: update_product_screen
tools.description:
Edit an existing brand asset: name, description, kind, use_when,
and the screenshot tags (screen_type, device, theme).

screen_id.description: Id of the brand asset from list_product_screens.

name.description: Human-readable name for the asset or run.

description.description: What the picture shows and what it is for, in your words. When set, Siren files the asset without reading it.

kind.description: Free-text kind: product photo, dashboard screenshot, packaging, logo, team photo.

use_when.description: When Siren should reach for this asset, e.g. "any post about the analytics page".

screen_type.description: Screen role: feature, hero, onboarding, settings, or marketing.

device.description: Device the screenshot was taken on: phone, tablet, desktop, or none.

theme.description: UI theme in the screenshot: light, dark, or unknown.

tools.name: delete_product_screen
tools.description: Remove a product screenshot from Brand DNA. Does not delete Brand Memory.

screen_id.description: Id of the brand asset from list_product_screens.

tools.name: upload_logo
tools.description: Set the workspace logo in Brand DNA. Every render uses it.

image_url.description: Public https URL of the logo (PNG, JPG or WebP).

image_base64.description: The logo bytes as base64, if you have no URL.

variant.description: light = the mark used on light backgrounds (the usual one); dark = the one for dark backgrounds.

tools.name: get_mascot
tools.description:
The workspace mascot: status (hero, keeping, frames, ready), the
hero picture, tries left, and every pose frame with its URL. Null
mascot = none yet.

tools.name: create_mascot
tools.description:
Start the brand mascot: from a description (note, kind) or from a
reference picture. Paid plans; 100 credits. Siren paints a hero in
about a minute; poll get_mascot, show the human, then mascot_step
keep (build the pose sheet) or retry (paint again, 3 tries). One
mascot per workspace.

note.description: Describe the character in the human's words: what it is, colours, personality, what to avoid. Up to 280 characters.

kind.description: auto (Siren picks from the brand), animal, creature, object, robot, food, or abstract.

style.description: Material: vinyl (default), clay, plush, wool, or glossy.

name.description: The mascot's name, if the human has one.

image_url.description: A reference picture of the mascot (https PNG/JPG/WebP). Siren paints it in the brand's style, keeping the character.

image_base64.description: The reference picture as base64, if you have no URL.

tools.name: mascot_step
tools.description:
Move the mascot on: keep the hero, paint it again, or add a pose.
Ask the human before keep, since it builds the whole sheet.

action.description: keep = build the pose sheet from this hero; retry = paint the hero again; pose = add one more pose to a built mascot.

note.description: For retry: what to change this time.

label.description: For pose: the pose in a few words, e.g. waving, holding a phone.

prompt.description: For pose: extra detail for the pose.

with_model.description: For pose: also make a 3D model of it (20 credits instead of 10).

tools.name: list_people
tools.description:
The people library: team faces Siren can put in stills (name,
role, team, status cropping or ready, round crop URL).

tools.name: add_person
tools.description:
Add a face to the people library. Siren crops it round in a few
seconds (status cropping, then ready). Only upload people who agreed.

image_url.description: Public https URL of a portrait (PNG, JPG or WebP), one face.

image_base64.description: The portrait as base64, if you have no URL.

role.description: Their role, e.g. Founder, Head of Design.

tools.name: delete_person
tools.description: Remove a face from the people library.

tools.name: set_webhook
tools.description:
Register a standing webhook: Siren POSTs every run event in this
workspace to the URL, so no agent has to poll. For one run only, pass
callback_url to create_campaign or render_asset instead. Each POST is
JSON {type, run_id, workspace_id, timestamp, data: {status, asset_url,
caption, error, output_type, campaign_id}} signed with the secret:
Standard Webhooks headers (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp,
webhook-signature) plus X-Signature-256 (hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw
body). The secret is shown once; keep it.

url.description: https URL that receives every run event in this workspace. Must resolve to a public address.

events.description: Any of run.completed, run.failed, run.posted. Omit for all three.

label.description: A name for it, e.g. "my agent".

secret.description: Signing secret, 16 to 80 characters. Omit and Siren mints one (returned once).

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description:
This workspace's standing webhooks: URL, events, and the last
delivery's status. Secrets are never shown again.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Stop a standing webhook.

tools.name: list_media
tools.description:
Photos and videos uploaded with upload_media, newest first, with
their URLs. Reuse a URL in create_campaign media or a film body.

tools.name: get_performance
tools.description:
How the posts did: totals (impressions, engagement, replies,
engagement rate) and the top posts with views, likes and replies.

tools.name: list_posts
tools.description:
Every post Siren sent or queued: platform, status, live URL, time,
and counts by status (posted, queued, failed).

limit.description: How many posts, 1 to 200. Newest first.

offset.description: Skip this many, to page back.

tools.name: buy_credits
tools.description:
Get a Stripe checkout link for more credits. Give the link to the
human; they pay on Stripe and the credits land in about a minute.
Nothing is charged by this call. Read the balance on get_account.

credits.description: Or a custom amount, 50 to 5000, at $0.20 each.

tools.name: ads_overview
tools.description:
The workspace's ads at a glance: spend today and this month against
the caps, live campaigns, connected ad accounts, every campaign with its
status and budget, and how many of Siren's suggestions are open. Call
first for anything about ads. Ads need Pro and the owner's ads switch
for this agent; a 403 `scope_ads` says where they turn it on.

tools.name: list_ad_campaigns
tools.description:
Every ad campaign: platform, status (draft, launching, paused,
active), daily budget, spend, clicks and results so far, plus the caps.

tools.name: get_ad_campaign
tools.description:
One ad campaign: its plan, the Page it runs as, and each ad with its
creative (asset_url), shape, copy and status. Poll this after make_ads
until every ad is ready, and after send_ads_to_platform until it is paused.

campaign_id.description: The ad campaign id from list_ad_campaigns or make_ads.

tools.name: ad_performance
tools.description:
How the ads did: totals, each campaign and each ad with spend,
impressions, clicks, results, click-through rate, cost per click and
cost per result. Money is in minor units (cents).

campaign_id.description: One campaign, or omit for all of them.

tools.name: ad_account_balance
tools.description:
What each ad account has spent, its spending limit, what's left
under it, and the platform's billing link. No app can add money to an
ad account: to top up, give the human billing_url.

tools.name: get_ad_caps
tools.description:
The spend caps every change must fit (a day and a month, across all
platforms), what's spent this month and the room left. Caps are raised
only by the human on the Ads page, never by an agent.

tools.name: list_ad_suggestions
tools.description:
Siren's open suggestions from its daily review (pause an ad with no
clicks, cut a costly one, give a winner more), each with its reason.

tools.name: ad_autopilot
tools.description:
Whether autopilot is on, what it may do by itself (pause a weak ad,
move a budget by up to 20%, inside the caps, once every 3 days per
campaign) and whether the plan allows it (Scale). Read only: the human
turns it on or off on the Ads page under Caps, never an agent.

tools.name: siren_help
tools.description:
Look up Siren itself: where something is in the app (pages, tabs,
buttons), how a feature works, plans, prices, credits and policies.
Returns up to 3 sections, each with its docs link and its place in the
app (e.g. Ads → Sales). Call it before telling the human where to click
or what something costs; if it returns nothing, say you're not sure and
point to https://mysiren.ai/docs. Read only.

query.description: The question in plain words, e.g. "where do I set up tracking", "can Spark make videos".

tools.name: ad_conversions
tools.description:
Sales tracking: whether the Siren tag has been seen on the site,
events this week, the Meta pixel, other platforms it sends to, Stripe,
and money made back in 30 days (minor units). Read only.

tools.name: tracking_setup
tools.description:
The whole Sales tracking setup as one Markdown brief for the site's
developer: the tag with this workspace's key (before </head> on every
page), the sign-up and purchase calls, consent, how to check it on
Ads → Sales, and where the tag goes in Next.js, React/Vite, Webflow,
Framer, WordPress and Shopify. Read only. Hand `markdown` over as it
is, or save it as SIREN-TRACKING.md.

tools.name: ad_audiences
tools.description:
The customer list and lookalike audiences on Meta: how many people
Siren knows, each audience's size and status. Read only; the human
makes audiences on the Ads page.

tools.name: ad_tests
tools.description:
Split tests: the ones running with each version's numbers, and
every verdict so far (the winner, its rate, how sure).

tools.name: ad_alerts
tools.description:
What needs the human now (rejected ads, spend spikes, account
problems, cap pauses), and what cleared in the last 30 days.

tools.name: boost_post
tools.description:
Boost any post Siren made: it becomes a Meta ad with its own
picture or video and caption, sent PAUSED. No credits; nothing spends
until go_live_ad_campaign and the human's yes. Pass the run_id, or a
post_id from list_posts (each row says boosted_campaign_id once it
is). With neither it lists the posts that did best lately so you can
pick one with the human. A post boosted before answers with that
campaign.

run_id.description: The post's run_id. Omit both ids to list the posts worth boosting.

post_id.description: Or a post id from list_posts; its run is boosted.

days.description: How long the ad runs once on, 1 to 90; 7 if omitted.

daily_budget_cents.description: Budget a day in minor units (2000 is $20), inside the caps.

tools.name: plan_ads
tools.description:
Siren drafts an ad plan from one prompt: goal, audience, budget
inside the caps, platforms and the ads to make (shape, hook, headline,
text). Nothing is made or spent. Show the human the plan, then make_ads.
With test, the versions split one budget and the verdict rule is set
before any spend.

prompt.description: The goal in plain words, e.g. "more Pro signups from US founders, $20 a day for two weeks".

test.description: Make the plan a split test: "hook" tests openings, "words" tests the text. Omit for a normal plan.

tools.name: make_ads
tools.description:
Make the plan's ads: a draft campaign per platform, and Siren renders
each ad (spends credits like any video or ad creative; tell the human
first). Nothing reaches the platform yet. Poll get_ad_campaign.

plan.description: The plan object from plan_ads, as is or edited.

tools.name: send_ads_to_platform
tools.description:
Send a ready draft to its platform: campaign, ad set and ads are
created PAUSED. Nothing spends until go_live_ad_campaign. Poll
get_ad_campaign: launching, then paused (or draft with launch_error).

campaign_id.description: A draft whose ads are all ready.

tools.name: go_live_ad_campaign
tools.description:
Turn a campaign on: real ad money starts. Always two calls. The
first returns status needs_confirm and a summary (per day, the most
this month, the caps): show it to the human word for word. Only when
they say yes, call again with the confirm code. Inside the caps only.

confirm.description: Omit the first time. Siren answers needs_confirm with a summary and a code; after the human says yes, call again with that code (good for 10 minutes).

tools.name: pause_ad_campaign
tools.description: Pause (turn off) a campaign now. Always allowed: it only stops spend.

reason.description: Why, in a few words, for the log.

tools.name: set_ad_budget
tools.description:
Change a campaign's daily budget, inside the caps. Lowering applies
now. Raising a live campaign answers needs_confirm first: show the
human the summary, then call again with the code.

daily_budget_cents.description: New budget a day in minor units: 2500 is $25.

confirm.description: Only for a raise on a live campaign: the code from the first call's needs_confirm.

tools.name: decide_ad_suggestion
tools.description:
Apply or dismiss one of Siren's suggestions. One that raises spend
answers needs_confirm first, like set_ad_budget.

approve.description: True to apply it, false to dismiss it.

confirm.description: Only when approving a suggestion that raises spend: the code from needs_confirm.

tools.name: list_brand_videos
tools.description:
The brand's own clips in Brand DNA: name, what each shows, when to
use it, tags, best moments with timestamps, poster and scan_status.

tools.name: upload_brand_video
tools.description:
Add a product demo, walkthrough or footage to Brand DNA. With only
the file, Gemini reads frames across the clip and writes what it
shows, when to use it, tags and the best moments (scan_status
scanning, then ready in about 15 seconds; poll list_brand_videos).
Films play it when a brief names it ("launch film with our checkout
demo"). Videos are for films; stills are painted from pictures.

url.description: Public https URL of the clip (MP4, MOV or WebM, up to 200 MB and 5 minutes).

base64.description: The clip bytes as base64, if you have no URL.

description.description: What the clip shows, in your words. When set, Siren files it without reading it.

use_when.description: When a film should play it, e.g. "any film about checkout".

tools.name: delete_brand_video
tools.description: Remove a clip from Brand DNA, file and poster included.

tools.name: delete_media
tools.description:
Delete one photo or video uploaded with upload_media. Only this
workspace's uploads; a film that already rendered keeps its copy.

url.description: The URL upload_media returned (or one from list_media).

tools.name: studio_templates
tools.description:
List Siren Studio's 33 React data-card types with family, description,
and body schema. Use this before studio_card so the body matches.

tools.name: studio_card
tools.description:
Render a Studio data card from a type + body. Deterministic React,
no paint. Optional live post after render. Returns run_id, image url,
and post url when posted.

output_type.description: One of the 33 Studio types from studio_templates, e.g. sale-notification.

body.description: Card fields for that type (amount, productName, …).

theme.description: dark or light. Omit to use the workspace default.

aspect.description: Canvas aspect, e.g. square-ig or wide-twitter.

post.description: If true, post the finished card to a connected account. Confirm with the user first.

platform.description: Connected channel if post is true: x, instagram, tiktok, linkedin, or youtube.

tools.name: studio_automate
tools.description:
Create a Studio profile on this API key. Returns generate curl and
inbound hook URLs (Stripe, GitHub, Uptime Kuma, Product Hunt, generic).
Passing delivery.social_account_ids turns on social delivery for the
profile — that publishes, so it requires Allow posting.

output_types.description: Studio types this profile may render.

tools.name: studio_schedule
tools.description: Render a Studio card then queue a ScheduledPost at scheduled_at.

platforms.description: x, instagram, tiktok, linkedin, youtube, or everything.

tools.name: studio_start
tools.description:
Start a video in Siren Studio from a description. Siren composes the
first take (about 10 to 20 seconds) and replies with what it made;
nothing is rendered or charged until studio_export. Returns the thread
and Siren's reply. The human sees the same thread in Studio and can
keep editing it there, or you can with studio_edit.

prompt.description: What to make, in plain words: "an App Store preview for our timer app, calm, show the station picker first". An App Store link works too.

template.description: Optional film id to start from (list_films names them). Omit and the director picks.

attachments.description: Optional files Siren reads and uses: URLs from upload_media (app screenshots, a logo, a reference picture, a short screen recording). Up to 6.

tools.name: studio_edit
tools.description:
Change a Studio video by asking, as the human would in the chat.
Only what the ask names changes; Siren replies with what it changed
(before and after) and the new version number. Waits up to about 25
seconds for the reply. No credits are spent until studio_export. A greeting
or a question gets an answer and no new version.

thread_id.description: The thread id from studio_start or studio_threads.

text.description: The change, in plain words: "shorter hook", "show the timer first", "use our orange", "make it vertical". May be empty when attachments say it all.

attachments.description: Optional files to use: URLs from upload_media (a screenshot to show, a logo to put in, a reference). Up to 6.

tools.name: studio_get
tools.description:
One Studio video: the chat so far (who said what, with diffs),
every version, and which version is current.

tools.name: studio_design_pack
tools.description:
The design tokens behind a Studio design, for building in the same
language: palette, fonts, radius and shadow as `tokens`; `css` (custom
properties plus a Tailwind v4 @theme block); `tailwind` (a v3 theme);
and `skill_md`, a short rules file to drop into the project so the
agent keeps to it.

Call it once the version has been exported, so `screens` carries the
rendered proofs and `exported` is true. Free and read-only: it reads a
design, it does not render one. Honest about scope: palette, fonts,
radius and shadow; no type scale or spacing ramp yet.

thread_id.description: The thread id from studio_start or studio_threads.

version.description: Version to read. Omit for the current one.

tools.name: studio_threads
tools.description:
The workspace's Studio videos, newest first: title, shelf, current
version, and whether a human or an agent started it.

tools.name: studio_export
tools.description:
Render a Studio design or video to files. Spends credits like any
render: a video 25 (platinum 50), a card 10, a set 10 a slide (an App
Store set of 6 is 60), charged once. A card or a set waits for the
render (about a minute) and returns every file in `asset_urls`, slide
1 first; a video returns the run id: poll get_run until it is terminal,
then show the human the file or post it with post_run.

version.description: Version to render. Omit for the current one.
